Allegations have emerged that the Police Service Commission promoted some retired Commissioners of Police to the rank of Assistant Inspectors-General of Police after they had left the Nigeria Police Force. Some police officers, who raised concerns over the promotions, alleged that the current board of the commission illegally elevated the retired officers, with four of them reportedly serving as aides to members of the board. The officers questioned the propriety of promoting individuals who had already retired from the police, particularly when some of them were allegedly working closely with members of the commission responsible for approving promotions. A source familiar with the allegations said, “The current board illegally promoted some retired CPs to AIGs’ rank after retirement from the police. Four of them are currently serving as aides to board members.” Another source said the promotions differ from the usual practice of elevating officers on the eve of retirement. The source said, “This is not that they were promoted and proceeded on retirement like we are used to. These ones had long been retired for one reason or the other, only for them to be promoted. One who was dismissed during Goodluck Jonathan tenure was last year promoted to DIG.” When contacted on Sunday, the Police Service Commission spokesman, Torty Kalu, defended the commission’s actions, saying officers who believed they were unfairly denied promotion while in service had the right to appeal. Tinubu promises better welfare, reforms for police Lagos woman allegedly stabs husband to death during altercation Tinubu promises better welfare, reforms for police He explained that the commission could review such appeals, investigate the circumstances surrounding delayed promotions and approve them where there was sufficient justification. “Before a decision is taken on any matter, there is always an investigation carried out on it. An investigation is carried out, due diligence, and they find out that you were not given justice,” Kalu said. He added that officers who obtained favourable court judgments directing their promotion could also benefit from backdated promotions, stressing that the commission was bound to obey such orders. On concerns that some beneficiaries were serving as aides to board members, Kalu argued that working with the commission did not disqualify anyone from enjoying rights available to other Nigerians. “For the fact that you are serving in the commission, you are a board member of the commission, doesn’t deprive you of your rights. You’re just like every other Nigerian who can benefit from where you deserve to be benefited,” he said. Kalu maintained that promotions were granted based on merit, adding that officers outside the commission had also benefited from successful appeals. “If somebody working with a board member of the commission benefited in view of maybe an appeal made and promotion given to the person, the fact that he’s working with the commission doesn’t stop him from enjoying that if he merits it. And if he doesn’t merit it, it wouldn’t be given,” he added. Solomon Odeniyi Solomon Odeniyi is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over six years of professional experience.
